title: From staffing request to final timesheet
subtitle: How Crewflow connects managers, venue managers and staff
evidence: Every claim is checked against PRODUCT_TRUTH.md (local code at f5187172).

segments.text: A venue needs a team for Friday. A manager needs to know who is booked. And staff need to know where to be, and what happens next.
Crewflow connects that whole journey, from the first request to the final timesheet.
Managers run their agency from the web console. Each manager has a private workspace for their own staff, venues and shifts.
Venue managers use the Crewflow app to ask for staff, and staff use the same app to see their offers, clock in, and check their hours.
It starts with the team. In the web console, the manager keeps a record for every staff member and every venue.
Each venue manager is linked to their venue, and the manager decides which staff they can work with. Here, Riley Chen runs Riverside House, with an assigned team.
In the app, Riley sees that team, and no one else.
On Tuesday, Riley needs four waiting staff for a wedding reception on Friday.
Riley chooses the venue, the role, the time and the break, then picks four people from the team.
If someone isn't normally available that day, Crewflow warns Riley before anything is sent.
The request goes to the manager for approval. Nothing reaches the staff yet.
In Venue Offers, the manager checks the request, can change who's on it, and approves.
Approval sends each person their own offer, with the venue, the time, and their estimated pay.
Priya opens hers and accepts. Because this shift came from an approved request, accepting books her straight away.
When a manager creates a shift directly, accepting reserves the place until the manager confirms it.
Either way, the manager can follow every person on the live staffing board.
On Friday, Priya's confirmed shift is in her app, with the notes for the day. Clock-in opens shortly before the start.
At the venue, she scans the shift's QR code, and Crewflow checks it on its server. Where a venue requires it, she also has to be on site.
Her shift is now live, timed by Crewflow's own clock, not her phone's.
When the shift ends, she scans the same code again to clock out.
After the shift, Riley opens the shift report.
Three people clocked in and out. Isla clocked in, but there's no clock-out, so Crewflow flags it, rather than guessing her hours.
Riley enters the correct time, gives a reason, and saves the correction.
Saving a correction isn't the same as approving it. Riley still marks each person's hours as reviewed, one by one.
Rating someone's performance is a separate, optional step.
Only when everyone is clocked out and reviewed does Finalise and send become available.
Riley confirms the break details, types their name to sign off, and sends. That locks the hours.
Crewflow then creates the final timesheet as a PDF, queues it for delivery, and shows when it has been sent.
The manager can open both the original and the signed timesheet on the web, and finished shifts move to History.
Back in the web console, the reviewed hours appear in Payroll, with the pay they add up to, ready for your payroll provider. Crewflow doesn't move any money.
Ratings from venue managers build up on each staff member's record.
And the calendar and dashboard show the week ahead, the hours worked, and how ready your next shift is.
Behind the scenes, the web console and the app work with one Crewflow service. It checks who you are, and which workspace you belong to, on every request.
Background jobs look after reminders, expiries and documents.
Request. Confirm. Work. Review. Timesheet. That's Crewflow.
To get started, open the guide for your role.
